title: Loaded sweet potatoes with chipotle black beans

items: 4 medium sweet potatoes (about 8 oz each), scrubbed
1 (15 oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 cup frozen or canned corn (drained if canned)
1 tsp adobo sauce from the can

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Line the sheet pan with foil, since the potatoes leak sticky syrup.
Prick each sweet potato 4–5 times with a fork, rub with the oil and sprinkle with salt. Bake 45–60 min, until a knife slides into the thickest part with no resistance.
About 10 min before the potatoes are done, combine the beans, corn, chipotle, adobo sauce and 2 Tbsp water in the saucepan. Warm over medium heat about 5 min, stirring, until hot. Season with salt.
Stir the sour cream, lime juice and a pinch of salt together. Add water 1 tsp at a time until it drizzles off a spoon.
Slit each potato lengthwise, push the ends toward the middle to open it and fluff the inside with a fork. Season with a pinch of salt.
Spoon the beans into the potatoes. Drizzle the lime sour cream in lines, then top with cotija, scallions and avocado. Serve with lime wedges.
tips: Short on time: microwave the pricked potatoes 8–10 min, turning once, until soft, then roast at 425°F for 10 min to crisp the skins.
Chipotles vary in heat. Start with half a pepper and taste before adding the rest.
Freeze the leftover chipotles flat in a zip-top bag so you can break off one at a time.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days, with the potatoes and beans stored apart from the sour cream and avocado. Reheat the potatoes and beans in the microwave 2–3 min, or at 350°F for 15 min, then add the cold toppings.
